Let \( A_1, A_2, A_3, \ldots \) be a sequence of finite nonempty sets of positive integers. Given that \( |A_i \cap A_j| = \gcd(i, j) \) for all (not necessarily distinct) positive integers \( i \) and \( j \), compute the minimum possible value of

\[
\sum_{d|250} \max A_d,
\]

where the sum ranges over all positive integer divisors \( d \) of 250.

(For a finite nonempty set \( S \), we define \( \max S \) as the largest element of \( S \).)


Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

Let \(M_d=\max A_d\). Taking \(i=j\) in the condition gives

\[
|A_i|=i,
\]

so in particular \(M_i\ge i\) for every \(i\).

Also, for any \(i,j\),

\[
|A_i\cup A_j|=|A_i|+|A_j|-|A_i\cap A_j|
=i+j-\gcd(i,j).
\]

Since \(A_i\cup A_j\subseteq \{1,2,\dots,\max(M_i,M_j)\}\), we must have

\[
\max(M_i,M_j)\ge i+j-\gcd(i,j).
\]

We will use this for the pairs \((2,5)\), \((10,25)\), and \((50,125)\), all of which divide \(250\).

### Lower bound

We have

\[
M_1\ge 1,\qquad M_{250}\ge 250.
\]

For \((2,5)\):

\[
M_2\ge 2,\quad M_5\ge 5,\quad \max(M_2,M_5)\ge 2+5-1=6.
\]

Thus \(M_2+M_5\ge 8\).

For \((10,25)\):

\[
M_{10}\ge 10,\quad M_{25}\ge 25,\quad \max(M_{10},M_{25})\ge 10+25-5=30.
\]

Thus \(M_{10}+M_{25}\ge 40\).

For \((50,125)\):

\[
M_{50}\ge 50,\quad M_{125}\ge 125,\quad \max(M_{50},M_{125})\ge 50+125-25=150.
\]

Thus \(M_{50}+M_{125}\ge 200\).

Therefore

\[
\sum_{d\mid 250} M_d
\ge 1+8+40+200+250=499.
\]

So the desired sum is at least \(499\).

### Construction attaining the bound

Use the standard totient construction. For each positive integer \(d\), create \(\varphi(d)\) distinct elements \(x_{d,1},\dots,x_{d,\varphi(d)}\), and define

\[
A_n=\{x_{d,k}: d\mid n,\ 1\le k\le \varphi(d)\}.
\]

Then

\[
|A_n|=\sum_{d\mid n}\varphi(d)=n
\]

and

\[
|A_i\cap A_j|
=\sum_{d\mid \gcd(i,j)}\varphi(d)
=\gcd(i,j).
\]

Now assign positive integer labels to these elements as follows:

\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
d & \varphi(d) & \text{labels}\\
\hline
1 & 1 & 1\\
2 & 1 & 2\\
5 & 4 & 3,4,5,6\\
10 & 4 & 7,8,9,10\\
25 & 20 & 11,\dots,30\\
50 & 20 & 31,\dots,50\\
125 & 100 & 51,\dots,150\\
250 & 100 & 151,\dots,250
\end{array}
\]

All remaining elements are labeled with distinct integers larger than \(250\). These extra elements do not affect any \(A_d\) with \(d\mid 250\).

With this labeling, the maxima are

\[
\begin{aligned}
M_1&=1,\\
M_2&=2,\\
M_5&=6,\\
M_{10}&=10,\\
M_{25}&=30,\\
M_{50}&=50,\\
M_{125}&=150,\\
M_{250}&=250.
\end{aligned}
\]

Their sum is

\[
1+2+6+10+30+50+150+250=499.
\]

Thus the minimum possible value is

\[
\boxed{499}
\]
